children: Proposed changes to insurance commissions added pressure on financial stocks already hit by higher global yields and crude prices

Financial stocks lost around Rs 1.12 lakh crore in combined market capitalisation during intraday trading on 24 September as investor sentiment weakened amid concerns over proposed insurance sector changes, higher global bond yields and rising crude prices. Twelve financial stocks recorded significant losses, with Bajaj Finance, PB Fintech, HDFC Bank and Axis Bank among the major contributors to the decline.

Bajaj Finance accounted for the largest erosion in market value at around Rs 29,000 crore, followed by PB Fintech at Rs 20,000 crore. HDFC Bank lost nearly Rs 15,000 crore, while Axis Bank shed around Rs 14,000 crore. Insurance linked companies were also hit after the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) proposed changes to insurers expenses and distributor commissions.

HDFC Life lost around Rs 7,600 crore in market capitalisation, while Max Financial and ICICI Prudential Life lost approximately Rs 6,800 crore and Rs 3,000 crore, respectively. Turtlemint's market value declined by around Rs 802 crore.

The proposed framework seeks tighter limits on expenses and commissions across insurance products and distribution channels. For life insurers, the expense of management limit is proposed to move towards 12.5 per cent within five years, while the corresponding limit for general insurers is proposed at 20 per cent. The consultation process is open until 25 October.

The proposed commission changes have also raised concerns over banks that earn income from selling insurance through their distribution networks. IIFL Research estimates that IndusInd Bank's bancassurance income exposure was equivalent to 79.3 per cent of its FY26 profit before tax.

Bandhan Bank followed at 30.8 per cent, RBL Bank at 28.5 per cent, Yes Bank at 19.3 per cent, Axis Bank at 12.5 per cent and HDFC Bank at 7.3 per cent. Brokerages have also assessed the potential earnings impact on insurance distributors. Jefferies estimated that a 10 per cent reduction in commission rates could lower earnings for PB Fintech and Turtlemint by 10 to 12 per cent.
The broader market sell off was compounded by higher US Treasury yields and Brent crude prices moving above 102 USD a barrel, increasing pressure on oil importing economies such as India.
